name: 5-Amino-1MQ
excerpt: Small-molecule NAMPT inhibitor studied for fat-cell metabolism and NAD+ pathway effects.
content: 5-Amino-1MQ is a quinolinium compound that inhibits nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT), an enzyme elevated in fat tissue and linked to obesity in animal models. Blocking NNMT raises intracellular nicotinamide and shifts adipocyte metabolism toward expenditure. Evidence is almost entirely rodent studies; no human trials exist. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 50mg/3ml the concentration is ~16.7 mg/ml; 50mg = 3 ml (full cartridge)

name: 5-Amino-1MQ (Oral)
excerpt: Oral tablet form of the NNMT inhibitor 5-Amino-1MQ.
content: Oral delivery of 5-Amino-1MQ. Oral bioavailability of this compound in humans is uncharacterised; all efficacy data is from injectable rodent studies. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: ACE-031
excerpt: Decoy receptor fusion protein that neutralises myostatin signalling, studied for muscle wasting.
content: ACE-031 is a soluble activin receptor IIB fusion protein that mops up myostatin and related ligands. Phase 2 trials in muscular dystrophy showed real lean-mass gains but were halted over bleeding and vascular side effects. It is a large recombinant protein, not a peptide. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Nosebleeds, telangiectasia, vascular effects seen in trials
meta.pen_dial: At 1mg/3ml the concentration is ~333 mcg/ml; dosing by weight

studies.citation: Phase 2 trial in muscular dystrophy (Acceleron, published 2010s)
studies.finding: Lean-mass gains demonstrated but halted over epistaxis/telangiectasia signals.

name: Acetic Acid 0.6%
excerpt: Diluent for reconstituting peptides sensitive to bacteriostatic water (e.g. IGF-1).
content: 0.6% acetic acid is the standard reconstitution vehicle for IGF peptides, which are unstable in bacteriostatic water. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Adamax (1032 Da)
excerpt: Semax analogue with an adamantane moiety, developed for cognitive neuroprotection.
content: Adamax is a Semax variant with an adamantane group, studied in Russian literature for BDNF modulation and neuroprotection. The two Adamax variants listed differ in molecular weight and thus in structure/purity claims. Human data is minimal. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Adamax (984 Da)
excerpt: Second Adamax variant (984 Da) of the adamantane-Semax family.
content: Alternate Adamax listing at 984 Da. Same family caveats: Russian-language preclinical data, no Western clinical trials. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: AHK-Cu
excerpt: Copper-binding tripeptide (Ala-His-Lys) studied for hair-follicle and collagen effects.
content: AHK-Cu is a copper tripeptide (alanine-histidine-lysine complexed with copper) studied mainly in hair-follicle research, where it promoted dermal papilla growth in vitro. Less established than GHK-Cu. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Topical use mainly; injectable protocols unverified
meta.pen_dial: Rarely used in cartridges; topical is more common

name: AICAR
excerpt: AMPK activator studied as an exercise mimetic in metabolic research.
content: AICAR (acadesine, 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide riboside) activates AMPK, the cell's energy-sensor, mimicking exercise-signalling in muscle. Famous from the 'exercise in a pill' mouse studies; no human performance or safety data at relevant doses. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal studies: 500 mg/kg range; no human regimen
meta.side_effects: Unknown in humans at active doses

studies.finding: AICAR improved endurance and oxidative muscle phenotype in sedentary mice — the 'exercise in a pill' study. No human performance data.

name: AICAR (Oral)
excerpt: Oral tablet form of the AMPK activator AICAR.
content: Oral AICAR; human oral bioavailability for AMPK-activating exposure is not established. Supplier flags conflicting evidence. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Alprostadil
excerpt: Prostaglandin E1 approved for erectile dysfunction (Caverject) — a genuine medicine with defined risks.
content: Alprostadil (PGE1) is an approved medicine for erectile dysfunction by intracavernosal injection or urethral gel. It works by direct smooth-muscle relaxation. Priapism (erection >4 hours) is a real emergency risk requiring defined dosing limits. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Priapism, penile pain, hypotension; contraindicated with priapism risk conditions
meta.pen_dial: At 20 mcg doses the pen is not the clinical delivery method

studies.finding: Intracavernosal PGE1 effective for ED in pivotal RCTs; priapism defined as dose-limiting risk.

name: Andarine (S-4) (Oral)
excerpt: Investigational SARM with partial-agonist profile; unapproved with vision reports at higher doses.
content: Andarine (S-4) is an early SARM with animal anabolic data. It is unapproved; a distinctive reported side effect is a yellow-tinge visual disturbance at higher doses, consistent with its ocular binding. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Suppression of natural testosterone; visual yellow tinge reported; lipid changes

name: AOD-9604
excerpt: Modified fragment of human growth hormone (amino acids 177-191) studied for lipolysis without growth effects.
content: AOD-9604 is a 15-amino-acid C-terminal fragment of HGH (tyrosine-tailed hGH 177-191) developed by Metabolic Pharmaceuticals for obesity. Animal and limited human work suggested fat-reduction effects without the diabetogenic or growth effects of whole HGH; the only published clinical trial failed to meet its endpoint. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Few reported; clinical trial data limited
meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 500 mcg ≈ 0.30 ml

studies.finding: The single published human trial failed to meet its endpoint — the honest headline for this compound.

name: ARA-290
excerpt: Erythropoietin-derived peptide (cibinetide) studied for nerve repair without blood effects.
content: Cibinetide is an 11-amino-acoid peptide derived from erythropoietin's helix B, retaining tissue-protective effects without stimulating red blood cells. Trials in small-fibre neuropathy showed improved corneal nerve measures — one of the better-evidenced research peptides. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 4mg ≈ 1.2 ml

name: B7-33
excerpt: H2-relaxin-derived peptide studied for antifibrotic effects.
content: B7-33 is a short peptide mimicking the antifibrotic actions of relaxin-2 via its receptor, studied in cardiac and pulmonary fibrosis models. Early-stage research only. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal-study dosing only; no human regimen

name: Benzyl Alcohol 0.9% (BAC)
excerpt: Bacteriostatic water preservative; the standard peptide reconstitution diluent.
content: Sterile water with 0.9% benzyl alcohol, which inhibits bacterial growth in reconstituted vials. The workhorse diluent for peptides. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.storage: Refrigerated; use within 28-30 days of puncture
meta.side_effects: Benzyl alcohol toxicity risk in neonates; irritation if concentrated

name: Botulinum Toxin A
excerpt: Neurotoxin protein approved for cosmetic and therapeutic use; one of the most toxic substances known.
content: Botulinum toxin type A blocks acetylcholine release at neuromuscular junctions. It is an approved medicine (Botox, and various biosimilars) for dystonia and aesthetics — and a lethal poison at roughly nanogram-per-kilogram scale. Research-grade vials carry the full risk of the real thing. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical dosing is unit-based by indication; no informal dosing is safe
meta.side_effects: Ptosis, dysphagia, weakness; systemic spread rare but serious

name: BPC-157

studies.citation: Sikiric et al., wound-healing rat studies (multiple papers, J Physiology-Pharmacology 2010s)
studies.finding: Consistent rat models of tendon, ligament, gut and wound healing; the entire evidence base is rodent.

studies.citation: Mechanism work (angiogenesis, FAK-Paxillin) from one mainly Croatian group
studies.finding: Largely single-group research; independent replication is thin.

bro_lore: Everywhere-repeated bro protocol: 250-500 mcg/day subcutaneous, 4 weeks on / 2 off. Origin: extrapolation from rat mg/kg dosing. No human dose-finding study exists.

name: BPC-157 (Oral)
excerpt: Oral formulation of the gastric-juice-derived healing peptide BPC-157.
content: BPC-157 is stable in gastric acid, which is the basis for oral formulations. Oral bioavailability in humans is unquantified; the healing data is almost entirely injectable-form animal work. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Few reported; long-term human safety unknown

studies.finding: Rodent oral dosing worked in models; human oral bioavailability unquantified.

name: BPC-157 + TB-500 Blend (Oral)
excerpt: Oral blend of the two most-used healing peptides.
content: Combines BPC-157 and TB-500 in oral form. No published data supports oral co-administration of either, let alone the blend; injectable animal data does not transfer to oral dosing. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.
bro_lore: Bro protocol: 500+500 mcg/day oral. Origin: forum folklore; no oral human data for either component.

name: BPC-157 Arg (Oral)
excerpt: Arginine-salt form of BPC-157 for oral delivery.
content: BPC-157 arginate is a salt form claimed to improve oral stability. Marketing claim aside, human oral pharmacokinetics remain unquantified. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: BPC-157 oral capsule
excerpt: Capsule form of oral BPC-157.
content: Encapsulated BPC-157 for oral use; same evidence caveats as other oral forms. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Bronchogen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for bronchial epithelium function.
content: Bronchogen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on bronchial epithelium tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Cagrilintide
excerpt: Long-acting amylin/calcitonin receptor co-agonist peptide studied for appetite suppression and weight loss.
content: Cagrilintide (Novo Nordisk) is an acylated 38-amino-acid amylin analogue activating amylin and calcitonin receptors, producing sustained appetite suppression. Phase 2 data showed robust weight loss, and phase 3 combination trials with semaglutide (CagriSema) are under way. It is not an approved medicine. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Nausea, injection-site reactions; long-term data pending
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 2.4mg ≈ 0.72 ml

studies.finding: 26 weeks: ~-6% weight loss at highest dose vs ~-1% placebo; CagriSema phase 3 trials ongoing.

name: Cagrilintide 10mg + Tirzepatide 10mg
excerpt: Blend of the amylin agonist cagrilintide with the dual GIP/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide.
content: A combination vial pairing two incretin-axis agents with complementary mechanisms (appetite suppression plus GIP/GLP-1 agonism). No published clinical data supports this specific co-formulation; combination dosing of unapproved peptides compounds the risk profile of both. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Additive GI effects expected; nausea, vomiting
meta.pen_dial: At 10+10mg/3ml each component is ~3333 mcg/ml; dosing is not established

name: Cardiogen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for cardiac tissue function.
content: Cardiogen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on cardiac tissue tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Cerebrolysin
excerpt: Porcine brain-derived peptide mixture used clinically in some countries for stroke and cognitive decline.
content: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides from pig brain, registered in several countries for stroke, TBI and vascular dementia. It has real randomised-trial literature (mostly from Eastern Europe and Asia) but is not approved in the UK/US. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical regimens abroad: 10-30 ml IV infusion courses (unverified for research vials)

studies.citation: Cochrane review (2021) on Cerebrolysin for acute ischaemic stroke
studies.finding: Signals of benefit vs placebo but low-certainty evidence; not approved in UK/US.

name: Chonluten
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for lung/liver function.
content: Chonluten is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on lung/liver tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: CJC-1295 + Ipamorelin
excerpt: Classic GHRH/GHRP pairing for a combined growth-hormone pulse.
content: Pairs a GHRH analogue with a selective GH secretagogue: one signals the pituitary to release, the other amplifies the pulse. Informally the most common GH-peptide stack. Neither component is approved for human use. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.reconstitution: Bacteriostatic water; 2ml per blend vial typical
meta.typical_dose: Reported protocols: 100 mcg of each 1-3x daily (unverified)
meta.side_effects: Water retention, numbness/tingling, cortisol effects at high doses
meta.pen_dial: At 5+5mg/3ml each component is ~1667 mcg/ml; 100 mcg of each ≈ 0.06 ml

bro_lore: Bro protocol: 100 mcg of each nightly before bed. Origin: GHRP forum dosing conventions from the 2000s.

name: CJC-1295 With DAC
excerpt: Long-acting GHRH analogue with albumin-binding tail extending its half-life to roughly a week.
content: CJC-1295 DAC is a modified GHRH(1-29) with a Drug Affinity Complex tail that binds albumin, stretching its half-life from minutes to ~6-8 days. It elevates GH and IGF-1 more continuously than the non-DAC form. Not approved for human use. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Reported protocols: 100 mcg daily or 300 mcg 2x weekly (unverified)
meta.side_effects: Water retention, flushing, fatigue; cortisol effects possible at high doses
meta.pen_dial: At 2mg/3ml the concentration is ~667 mcg/ml; 100 mcg ≈ 0.15 ml

studies.finding: Human trial showed prolonged GH/IGF-1 elevation for days from single injection; development did not continue.

name: CJC-1295 Without DAC
excerpt: GHRH analogue also known as mod GRF 1-29 — a short, natural-pulse GH releaser.
content: CJC-1295 without DAC (mod GRF 1-29) is the 29-amino-acid GHRH analogue without the albumin tail, giving a half-life of ~30 minutes and a natural GH pulse shape. Usually paired with a GHRP. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Milder than DAC form; flushing, water retention
meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 100 mcg ≈ 0.06 ml

name: Cortagen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for vascular/cognitive support function.
content: Cortagen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on vascular/cognitive support tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Crystagen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for immune system function.
content: Crystagen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on immune system tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Dermorphin
excerpt: Extremely potent opioid peptide from frog skin; dangerous even at microgram scale.
content: Dermorphin is a heptapeptide from Phyllomedusa frog skin, ~30-40x more potent than morphine at mu-opioid receptors. It has no legitimate human use; the supplier's own dose-related warning is warranted. Respiratory depression risk is severe. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Severe respiratory depression, dependence; naloxone-reversible in principle
meta.pen_dial: Microgram-scale only; not appropriate for pen dosing

name: Dihexa (Oral)
excerpt: Angiotensin IV analogue with hepatotoxicity concerns, studied for cognitive enhancement.
content: Dihexa is an angiotensin IV analogue (N-hexanoic-Tyr-Ile-(6)aminohexanoic amide) showing synaptogenic effects ~1000x more potent than BDNF by some measures in animal studies. Hepatotoxicity was observed in animal work — the reason development did not proceed. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal-study dosing only; no human regimen
meta.side_effects: Hepatotoxicity signals in animals; no human safety data

name: DSIP
excerpt: Delta sleep-inducing peptide studied for sleep architecture and stress.
content: DSIP (Trp-Ala-Gly-Gly-Asp-Ala-Ser-Gly-Glu) was isolated from rabbit brain in the 1970s. Human studies (small, dated) reported improved sleep onset and reduced opioid withdrawal symptoms; the literature never matured into a therapy. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 200 mcg ≈ 0.12 ml

studies.citation: Small dated human studies (1970s-80s, sleep architecture)
studies.finding: Mixed small-sample results on sleep onset; never matured into therapy.

name: Eloralintide
excerpt: Incretin receptor agonist in early clinical development for weight management.
content: Eloralintide is a next-generation incretin receptor agonist in early clinical development (Hengrui/Lilly lineage data is limited in public literature). Public information on receptor selectivity and dosing is sparse; treat all circulating protocols as unverified. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

studies.citation: Khavinson et al. (St Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology)
studies.finding: Reported telomerase activation and telomere elongation in cell cultures and melatonin restoration in rodents/humans. Unreplicated in Western literature.

name: EPO
excerpt: Erythropoietin — approved medicine for anaemia with serious misuse risks (thrombosis, Hct abuse).
content: EPO is a glycoprotein hormone approved for anaemia of kidney disease and chemotherapy. Misuse to raise haematocrit (doping) thickens blood and raises stroke/heart-attack risk — deaths in endurance sport are documented. Research-grade vials are not pharmaceutical grade. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical regimens are IU/kg-based; no safe informal dosing
meta.side_effects: Hypertension, thrombosis, stroke risk; contraindicated with uncontrolled hypertension
meta.pen_dial: IU-dosed; 3000 IU at 3000IU/3ml = 1 ml per dose

studies.finding: Established clinical benefit in defined anaemia; misuse (doping) raises thrombotic risk — documented deaths.

name: Fat Blaster
excerpt: Injectable blend of L-carnitine, MIC (methionine, inositol, choline), B6 and NADH.
content: A 'lipotropic' injection blend combining L-carnitine (fatty-acid transport) with MIC components and B-vitamin cofactors. These mixes are used in aesthetic clinics; controlled evidence for meaningful fat loss is weak. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinic protocols: 1-2 ml weekly into fatty tissue (unverified)
meta.pen_dial: Supplied as 10 ml ready-to-use solution, not cartridges

name: FOXO4-DRI
excerpt: D-retro-inverso peptide that disrupts FOXO4-p53 interaction; studied as a senolytic.
content: FOXO4-DRI is an all-D-amino-acid peptide that interferes with the FOXO4-p53 complex, pushing senescent cells into apoptosis — the basis of the 2016 senolytic mouse studies. No human data exists; D-peptide long-term effects are unknown. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal studies: mg/kg range; no human regimen
meta.side_effects: Unknown; senescent-cell loss in renewing tissues is a theoretical risk

studies.finding: Disrupting FOXO4-p53 with the DRI peptide cleared senescent cells in progeroid and naturally aged mice, restoring fitness. No human data.

name: GAZ Blend
excerpt: Vitamin/nutrient complex blend (402.5 mg/ml).
content: Wellness injection blend; no clinical evidence base for the fixed formulation. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: GGH Blend
excerpt: Skin/hair/nail vitamin-peptide blend (402 mg/ml).
content: Multi-component wellness blend; no clinical evidence base for the fixed formulation. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: GHK Basic
excerpt: GHK tripeptide without copper — the base sequence of GHK-Cu.
content: GHK (glycyl-histidyl-lysine) without the copper ion retains some signalling activity but most of the published skin data involves the copper complex. Used in cosmetic formulations. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Cosmetic topical use; injectable protocols unverified
meta.pen_dial: Rarely used in cartridges; topical is more common

name: GLOW
excerpt: Blend of TB-500, BPC-157 and GHK-Cu.
content: Three-peptide healing/skin blend. No published clinical data for the co-formulation; component pharmacology applies. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Glutathione
excerpt: Endogenous tripeptide antioxidant; injectable use for skin-brightening is clinic folklore.
content: Glutathione (Glu-Cys-Gly) is the cell's principal non-protein antioxidant. Oral bioavailability is poor; IV use for skin lightening is popular in clinics but has weak evidence and occasional hypersensitivity reactions. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.reconstitution: Bacteriostatic water; often IV in clinics
meta.side_effects: Hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis (rare); long-term high-dose effects unknown

studies.citation: Watanabe et al., small RCTs on oral glutathione skin effects (2019)
studies.finding: Weak/small-sample evidence for skin lightening; IV clinic use outpaces evidence.

name: GW-501516 (Cardarine) (Oral)
excerpt: PPARδ agonist studied for endurance; development stopped over cancer findings in animals.
content: Cardarine is not a SARM but a PPAR-delta agonist that switches muscle to fat oxidation. GSK abandoned development after long-term animal studies showed rapid cancer development in multiple tissues. That finding is the single most important fact about this compound. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Carcinogenicity signals in animal studies; HDL suppression

studies.citation: Long-term rodent carcinogenicity studies (GSK development programme)
studies.finding: Rapid tumour development in multiple tissues ended development — the key fact about this compound.
PPARdelta activation improved endurance in mice ('marathon mouse').

name: HCG
excerpt: Human chorionic gonadotropin — approved medicine used off-label for testosterone induction.
content: HCG mimics LH and stimulates testicular testosterone production. It is an approved fertility medicine; informal use to maintain testicular function during anabolic-steroid use is unapproved. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical regimens: 500-5000 IU by indication (unverified for informal use)
meta.side_effects: Gynaecomastia, water retention, HPTA suppression; headache
meta.pen_dial: IU-dosed; 5000 IU at 5000IU/3ml = 1 ml per 1667 IU

studies.citation: Approved fertility literature; testosterone-induction RCTs (e.g. Lipshultz et al.)
studies.finding: Effective LH-mimetic for hypogonadism and fertility indications.

name: Healthy Hair Skin Nails
excerpt: B-vitamin, biotin and folic acid complex for skin/hair/nail support.
content: Vitamin-complex injection blend; oral supplementation has equivalent evidence for the same ingredients at lower cost and risk. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Hexarelin
excerpt: Powerful synthetic GHRP producing the largest GH pulses of its class.
content: Hexarelin is a hexapeptide GHRP (His-D-2MeTrp-Ala-Trp-D-Phe-Lys-NH2) producing stronger GH release than GHRP-6 or ipamorelin, but with less selectivity — cortisol and prolactin can rise at higher doses. Desensitisation occurs with repeated dosing. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 100 mcg ≈ 0.06 ml

studies.finding: Human GH-dose-response established in pharmacology studies; desensitisation documented.

name: HGH 191AA (Somatropin)
excerpt: Recombinant 191-amino-acid human growth hormone; an approved medicine with well-characterised risks when misused.
content: Somatropin is identical to endogenous human GH and is an approved medicine for GH deficiency and wasting disorders. Misuse for physique or anti-ageing purposes carries genuine risks: insulin resistance, oedema, carpal tunnel, and possible promotion of malignancy. Research-grade vials are not pharmaceutical grade. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Approved paediatric/adult regimens: IU-based by weight; informal 2-4 IU daily (unverified)
meta.side_effects: Insulin resistance, oedema, joint pain, carpal tunnel; contraindicated with active malignancy
meta.pen_dial: At 10IU/1ml insulin-style dosing; 1 IU = 0.1 ml of a 10IU/ml solution

studies.citation: Blackman et al., JAMA 2002 (GH in healthy older adults)
studies.finding: GH reduced fat mass and increased lean mass but worsened glucose and caused frequent adverse effects — key misuse-relevant trial.
Established benefits exist only for defined deficiency states.

name: HGH Fragment 176-191
excerpt: Synthetic fragment of the HGH C-terminus studied for lipolytic effects without growth or glycaemic action.
content: hGH 176-191 (AOD-9604's parent fragment) is the terminal 16 residues of human growth hormone, studied since the 1980s for isolated lipolytic activity. Evidence is largely in vitro and animal; human data never matured into an approved product. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 500 mcg ≈ 0.30 ml

bro_lore: Bro protocol: 250-500 mcg/day. Origin: fragment-HGH folklore; the parent fragment never completed human development.

name: HMG
excerpt: Human menopausal gonadotropin (menotropin) — LH/FSH fertility medicine.
content: HMG provides both LH and FSH activity and is an approved fertility medicine for ovarian stimulation and male hypogonadism. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Ovarian hyperstimulation in women; injection-site reactions

name: Humanin
excerpt: Mitochondrial-derived 24-amino-acid peptide studied for cytoprotection and metabolic effects.
content: Humanin is a 24-residue peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA, cytoprotective in models of neurodegeneration, cardiac ischaemia and metabolic stress. Early-stage human data (small biomarker studies). This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.3 ml

studies.finding: Neuroprotective and cardioprotective in cell/animal models; human data minimal.

name: Hyaluronic Acid
excerpt: Naturally occurring glycosaminoglycan used clinically for joint and dermal filling.
content: Hyaluronic acid is a high-molecular-weight glycosaminoglycan present in connective tissue; approved products exist for osteoarthritis injection and dermal filling. Cross-linking determines duration; research-grade material is not a clinical filler. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical: joint 20 mg per injection; filler by product
meta.side_effects: Injection-site swelling, granuloma (rare); vascular occlusion risk in face

name: IGF-1 LR3
excerpt: Long-acting insulin-like growth factor 1 analogue (83 residues) studied for muscle growth and recovery.
content: IGF-1 LR3 is human IGF-1 with an arginine substitution and a 13-amino-acid N-terminal extension, giving ~50x receptor affinity and a much longer half-life. It drives anabolic and anti-catabolic signalling; hypoglycaemia is the acute risk. Not approved for human use. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.reconstitution: Acetic acid 0.6% then buffer, or bacteriostatic water
meta.side_effects: Hypoglycaemia risk, injection-site irritation, potential cancer-promotion concerns
meta.pen_dial: At 1mg/3ml the concentration is ~333 mcg/ml; 50 mcg ≈ 0.15 ml

studies.citation: Preclinical muscle/anabolic studies of IGF-1 variants (1990s)
studies.finding: Potent anabolic signalling in animal and cell models; no human LR3 trials.

bro_lore: Bro protocol: 20-50 mcg post-workout. Origin: bodybuilding folklore from 2000s forums; hypoglycaemia risk often understated.

studies.finding: Selective GH release with minimal cortisol/prolactin effects in human pharmacology studies — among the cleaner GHRP profiles.

name: KissPeptin-10
excerpt: Hypothalamic peptide that drives GnRH release — a master switch of reproductive hormone pulsing.
content: Kisspeptin-10 is a decapeptide from the kisspeptin family, acting upstream of GnRH to pulse gonadotropin release. Genuine clinical-research literature exists (including human trials for IVF and hypogonadism); informal use risks disrupting the HPG axis. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 100 mcg ≈ 0.03 ml

studies.citation: Jayasena et al. (Hammersmith), human kisspeptin trials 2010s
studies.finding: Human RCT work showing gonadotropin stimulation and possible IVF use; genuinely human-based literature.

name: KLOW
excerpt: Blend of TB-500, BPC-157, KPV and GHK-Cu.
content: Four-component blend stacking healing peptides with the anti-inflammatory tripeptide KPV. No published clinical data for the co-formulation. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: KPV
excerpt: Anti-inflammatory tripeptide derived from the C-terminus of alpha-MSH.
content: KPV (Lys-Pro-Val) is the anti-inflammatory core of alpha-MSH, active at peripheral sites without melanogenic effects. Studied in models of colitis and skin inflammation; human data is minimal. Stable enough for oral use, which is the basis of the oral products. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 500 mcg ≈ 0.15 ml

studies.finding: Anti-inflammatory in rodent models of colitis; no human trials.

name: KPV (Oral)
excerpt: Oral form of the anti-inflammatory tripeptide KPV.
content: Oral KPV targets gut inflammation in models; human oral bioavailability data is minimal. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: L-Carnitine
excerpt: Fatty-acid transport cofactor used for energy and recovery.
content: L-carnitine shuttles fatty acids into mitochondria. It is a standard supplement with modest evidence for some metabolic parameters; injectable use in clinics is common but adds no proven benefit over oral for most purposes. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Injection-site pain, fishy odour at high doses, GI upset

studies.citation: Meta-analyses of L-carnitine supplementation (e.g. Poole et al., 2018)
studies.finding: Modest effects on weight and metabolic markers in supplementation trials; injectable advantage over oral is not established.

name: L-Carnitine (Liquid)
excerpt: Liquid L-carnitine (500 mg/ml) for injection.
content: Liquid carnitine preparation; same profile as the 600 mg/ml product. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Lemon Bottle (liquid)
excerpt: Fat-dissolving injectable solution containing riboflavin, bromelain and lecithin.
content: Lemon Bottle is a Korean aesthetic-clinic lipolytic solution. Its active composition (riboflavin, bromelain, lecithin) is not an approved pharmaceutical product in the UK/EU, and published safety and efficacy data is minimal. Typically micro-injected into submental or body fat by practitioners. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: LGD-4033 (Ligandrol) (Oral)
excerpt: Non-steroidal SARM in dose-ranging trials for muscle wasting.
content: Ligandrol is a selective androgen receptor modulator with phase 1 data showing lean-mass increases at 1-3 mg/day. Like all SARMs it is unapproved, suppresses natural testosterone, and research tablets have unverified content. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Suppression of natural testosterone, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation; long-term data absent

studies.finding: 1.0-2.0 mg/day for 21 days increased lean mass dose-dependently with testosterone suppression at higher doses.

name: Lipo Mino Mix
excerpt: MIC-plus-carnitine lipotropic injection blend.
content: A lipotropic blend (methionine, inositol, choline plus L-carnitine) used in aesthetic weight-loss protocols. Evidence for efficacy beyond modest energy-metabolism support is weak. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Lipo-C 120
excerpt: L-carnitine with methionine, choline and B5 lipotropic blend.
content: Classic 'Lipo-C' formulation: L-carnitine, methionine, choline, B5. Same caveats as other lipotropic blends — clinic popularity, thin evidence. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Lipo-C 216
excerpt: L-carnitine, MIC and B-complex lipotropic blend.
content: Lipo-C variant with added B-complex. Clinic lipotropic injection; efficacy evidence weak. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Lipo-C Focus
excerpt: High-concentration lipotropic blend (425 mg/ml).
content: Concentrated lipotropic mix for clinic use. Same evidence caveats apply. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Liraglutide
excerpt: GLP-1 receptor agonist (Victoza/Saxenda) approved for diabetes and weight management.
content: Liraglutide is a once-daily acylated GLP-1 analogue approved as Victoza (diabetes) and Saxenda (obesity), with extensive trial data (SCALE programme). It is a genuine medicine; research-grade vials are not pharmaceutical grade. Dose escalation matters — starting high causes severe GI effects. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.reconstitution: Bacteriostatic water; supplied solution in pens
meta.side_effects: Nausea, vomiting, gallbladder events; MTC/MEN2 contraindications
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 1.8mg ≈ 0.54 ml

studies.citation: SCALE Obesity: Pi-Sunyer et al., NEJM 2015
studies.finding: 56-week RCT, 3.0 mg daily: -8.4% vs -2.8% placebo.

name: Livagen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for liver function.
content: Livagen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on liver tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Matrixyl
excerpt: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-4 (Pal-KTTKS), a cosmetic collagen-signalling peptide.
content: Matrixyl is palmitoyl pentapeptide-4, a cosmetic peptide with published (industry-funded) clinical work showing modest wrinkle improvement. It is a topical cosmetic ingredient, not an injectable. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Cosmetic topical use; 10 mg vials for DIY serums

name: Mazdutide
excerpt: GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist in Chinese phase 3 trials for obesity and diabetes.
content: Mazdutide (IBI362, Innovent) is a once-weekly GLP-1 and glucagon receptor dual agonist in phase 3 development in China, with published phase 2 data showing double-digit weight loss. Not approved anywhere yet. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: GLP-1-class GI effects; glucagon effects possible
meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 5mg = 3 ml (full cartridge)

studies.citation: Phase 2 RCTs (Innovent/Lilly programme, published in Lancet-family journals)
studies.finding: Weekly dosing produced double-digit weight-loss signals in Chinese phase 2; phase 3 ongoing.

name: Melanotan-1
excerpt: Linear melanocortin-1 agonist (afamelanotide) approved in the EU for erythropoietic protoporphyria.
content: Afamelanotide (Scenesse) is a linear alpha-MSH analogue selective for MC1R, approved in the EU for light-protection in erythropoietic protoporphyria. It tans with fewer off-target effects than Melanotan II. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Approved: 16 mg implant every 2 months; informal protocols unverified
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.3 ml

studies.citation: Scenesse (afamelanotide) EU approval programme for EPP
studies.finding: EU approval (2014) for light protection in erythropoietic protoporphyria based on RCTs.

name: Melanotan-2
excerpt: Unapproved melanocortin agonist for tanning; known for nausea and blood-pressure effects.
content: Melanotan II is a cyclic melanocortin receptor agonist inducing pigmentation and (via MC4R) appetite and sexual effects. It has never been approved; nausea, flushing, spontaneous erections and new-mole concerns are documented in users. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Nausea (common), flushing, BP changes, new pigmented lesions
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 250 mcg ≈ 0.075 ml

name: Methylcobalamin (Vitamin B12)
excerpt: Active coenzyme form of vitamin B12 for energy protocols.
content: Methylcobalamin is the active methyl-donor form of B12, used clinically for B12 deficiency. Injectable use for non-deficient 'energy' has weak evidence. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical: 1 mg IM per protocol; informal weekly (unverified)

name: Methylene Blue (Oral)
excerpt: Mitochondrial dye and MAO inhibitor used off-label as a nootropic; serotonin-risk profile.
content: Methylene blue is a redox cycler and potent MAO-A inhibitor. It has legitimate medical uses (methemoglobinemia, surgical dye) and research history in psychiatry, but combining it with SSRIs/SNRIs risks serotonin syndrome — a real, documented interaction. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs/SNRIs; blue urine; GI effects

name: MK-677 (Ibutamoren) (Oral)
excerpt: Oral non-peptide ghrelin-receptor agonist that raises GH and IGF-1 chronically.
content: Ibutamoren is an oral growth-hormone secretagogue mimicking ghrelin; trials showed sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation and modest lean-mass gain, with increased appetite and water retention as common effects. It is not a SARM, not a peptide, and not approved. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Increased appetite, water retention, fasting glucose elevation, lethargy

studies.citation: Nass et al., 2-year RCT in older adults (2008)
studies.finding: Sustained GH/IGF-1 elevation but no significant functional improvement; fasting glucose rose.
Increased stage IV sleep and GH pulses in young volunteers.

name: MOTS-C
excerpt: Mitochondrial-derived peptide studied for metabolic regulation and exercise mimetics.
content: MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA, acting as an exercise-induced metabolic regulator via AMPK and folate-cycle modulation. Human data is early (obesity trial work); popular in longevity circles ahead of evidence. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 10mg = 3 ml (full cartridge)

studies.citation: Cohen/Lee lab work incl. small human exercise trials (2015-2023)
studies.finding: Exercise-induced MOTS-c elevation in humans; obesity trial work early-stage.

name: NA Epithalon Amidate
excerpt: Amidated Epithalon variant with claimed longer action.
content: Amidated analogue of the Epithalon tetrapeptide; same Khavinson lineage and evidence caveats, with the modification claimed to extend stability. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 5mg/3ml the concentration is ~1667 mcg/ml; 5mg = 3 ml (full cartridge)

name: NA Selank Amidate
excerpt: Amidated Selank variant with claimed longer action.
content: N-acetylated/amidated Selank analogue claimed to extend stability and duration. Same evidence base as Selank (Russian clinical use, minimal Western data). This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: NA Semax Amidate
excerpt: Amidated Semax variant with claimed longer action.
content: Amidated Semax analogue; the modification is claimed to resist peptidase degradation. No Western clinical data. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: NAD+ 100mg + MOTS-C 10mg + 5-Amino-1MQ 10mg
excerpt: Triple metabolic blend: NAD+, MOTS-c and 5-Amino-1MQ.
content: Stacks three metabolic-research compounds with complementary but individually unproven human injectable data. Blend has no published clinical support. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: NAD+ Oil
excerpt: Topical/oil-based NAD+ preparation.
content: NAD+ is not dermally bioavailable to any established degree; topical preparations are speculative. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Orforglipron (Oral)
excerpt: Non-peptide oral GLP-1 receptor agonist in phase 3 development (Lilly).
content: Orforglipron is a small-molecule oral GLP-1 agonist — the peptide-free future of the class — in phase 3 trials with published phase 2 weight-loss data. Research-grade oral tablets are not the clinical formulation; no approved dosing exists yet. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

studies.citation: Phase 2 RCT: Wharton et al., NEJM 2023
studies.finding: 36 weeks: up to -14.7% at 45 mg daily in obesity; phase 3 ongoing.

name: Ostarine (MK-2866) (Oral)
excerpt: One of the most-studied SARMs, trialled for muscle wasting and injury recovery.
content: Ostarine has multiple published clinical trials showing lean-mass preservation at 1-3 mg/day. It remains unapproved; testosterone suppression occurs dose-dependently, and sports testing detects it readily. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Suppression of natural testosterone, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation; long-term data absent

studies.citation: Basaria/Dobs et al., JCEM 2013 (enobosarm phase 2, older adults)
studies.finding: 1-3 mg/day increased lean mass and stair-climb power vs placebo.

name: Ovagen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for liver function.
content: Ovagen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on liver tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Oxytocin Acetate
excerpt: Naturally occurring neuropeptide used clinically for labour induction; informally for bonding and social effects.
content: Oxytocin is a nine-amino-acid neuropeptide, approved for labour induction and postpartum haemorrhage control. Informal use for social/bonding/sexual effects has weak human evidence, and chronic dosing may blunt natural receptor responses. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical: IU-based infusion; informal intranasal 24-40 IU (unverified)
meta.side_effects: Uterine contraction (dangerous outside labour), hyponatraemia with high-volume dosing
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 50 mcg ≈ 0.015 ml

studies.finding: Established for labour induction; intranasal social/sexual effects have small inconsistent trials.

name: P21
excerpt: CNTF-derived peptide studied for neurogenesis and cognitive repair.
content: P21 is a small peptide derived from ciliary neurotrophic factor (via the CNTF fragment pathway from Israeli research), studied in animal models of Alzheimer's and brain injury. Early-stage research; no human trials. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal-study dosing only; no human regimen

name: P21 (Adamantane)
excerpt: Adamantane-modified P21 variant for enhanced CNS delivery.
content: Adamantane group added to improve blood-brain-barrier penetration. Same early-stage status as P21 itself. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal-study dosing only; no human regimen

name: Pancragen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for pancreas function.
content: Pancragen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on pancreas tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: PE-22-28
excerpt: Periostin-derived peptide studied for depression and neurogenesis.
content: PE-22-28 is a 7-residue peptide derived from periostin, identified in screens for antidepressant-like effects via TREK-1 channel modulation. Promising in mice; no human data. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Animal-study dosing only; no human regimen

name: Pinealon
excerpt: Short tripeptide (Glu-Asp-Arg) bioregulator studied for pineal and cognitive function.
content: Pinealon (Glu-Asp-Arg) is a Khavinson-series tripeptide bioregulator claimed to modulate pineal melatonin production and protect neurons. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 2mg ≈ 0.3 ml

name: PNC27
excerpt: Peptide that targets cancer-cell membranes via p53/HDM2 disruption; early-stage oncology research.
content: PNC27 is a peptide designed to kill cancer cells by binding HDM2 on their membranes and inducing necrosis — a laboratory concept, not a therapy. Any informal use is pure speculation with real danger. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Prostamax
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for prostate function.
content: Prostamax is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on prostate tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

studies.citation: Phase 3 RECONNECT: Kingsberg et al., Obstet Gynecol 2019
studies.finding: Significant improvement in HSDD endpoints in premenopausal women; FDA approval as Vyleosi followed (2019).

name: PTD-DBM
excerpt: Wnt-signalling peptide studied for hair growth via the hair-follicle stem-cell niche.
content: PTD-DBM is a cell-penetrating peptide mimicking the Dishevelled-binding motif, activating Wnt/beta-catenin signalling in hair-follicle research. Animal data is promising; human data is absent. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Reported protocols: topical or 1-5 mg injectable (unverified)

name: RAD-140 (Oral)
excerpt: Potent SARM developed for breast-cancer and wasting research.
content: Testolone (RAD-140) is a strong SARM from Radius Health's oncology programme. No completed human trials are published; preclinical data shows tissue-selective anabolic effects. Unapproved and frequently under-dosed or contaminated in research products. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Suppression of natural testosterone, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation; long-term data absent

studies.finding: 24-week RCT: mean -17.5% at 12 mg vs -1.6% placebo; phase 3 ongoing, no approval anywhere.

name: Retatrutide + Cagrilintide
excerpt: Blend of the GLP-1/GIP/glucagon triple agonist retatrutide with the amylin agonist cagrilintide.
content: Combines two unapproved incretin-axis agonists with complementary mechanisms. No published data supports the fixed blend; both components individually lack long-term human safety data. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Additive GI effects expected; nausea, vomiting

name: S-23 (Oral)
excerpt: Very potent investigational SARM explored for male hormonal contraception.
content: S-23 is among the strongest SARMs studied, investigated as a male contraceptive because it suppresses the HPG axis hard. That same suppression makes it the riskiest of the class for libido and hormonal crash after use. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Marketed as contraceptive-strength suppression: severe HPG shutdown expected

studies.citation: Russian registration studies (Institute of Molecular Genetics RAS)
studies.finding: Registered in Russia as an anxiolytic; GABA-mimetic and BDNF effects shown in Russian-language studies. Western replication absent.

name: Selank + Semax
excerpt: Combined Russian nootropic/anxiolytic peptide blend.
content: Pairs the anxiolytic Selank with the nootropic Semax. Both have Russian registration individually; the fixed blend has no published clinical support. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

studies.finding: 68-week RCT, 2.4 mg weekly: mean -14.9% body weight vs -2.4% placebo.
Sustained weight loss to 104 weeks (-15.2% vs 2.6% placebo).

name: Semaglutide oral tablet
excerpt: Oral formulation of semaglutide (the Rybelsus approach) in research-grade tablet form.
content: Oral semaglutide requires absorption enhancers (SNAC in the approved product Rybelsus) and specific fasting conditions; generic research tablets have no bioavailability guarantee. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Approved oral regimen: 3-14 mg daily with water on empty stomach

studies.finding: Registered in Russia for stroke and optic nerve disease; BDNF modulation shown in Russian-language work. Western replication absent.

name: Sermorelin Acetate
excerpt: GHRH(1-29) analogue that stimulates natural, pulsatile growth-hormone release.
content: Sermorelin is the shortest fully-active fragment of GHRH, once FDA-approved for diagnostic GH testing in children. It promotes natural GH pulsation rather than replacing GH. Used in longevity clinics ahead of strong evidence. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 9mg/3ml the concentration is ~3000 mcg/ml; 500 mcg ≈ 0.17 ml

studies.finding: Once FDA-approved for GH stimulation testing; current clinical role is minimal.

bro_lore: Longevity-clinic protocol: 200-500 mcg before bed. Origin: clinic marketing extrapolated from diagnostic dosing.

name: SHRED
excerpt: High-concentration (350 mg/ml) lipotropic injection blend.
content: Multi-component lipotropic blend at high concentration for clinic protocols; efficacy evidence weak. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: SLU-PP-332
excerpt: Synthetic ERRγ agonist studied as an 'exercise mimetic' for metabolic and endurance effects.
content: SLU-PP-332 is an estrogen-related receptor gamma (ERRγ) agonist from academic labs (Florida), showing improved endurance and fat metabolism in mice. No human data exists at all; it is a research chemical. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.reconstitution: Bacteriostatic water or DMSO vehicle in studies
meta.typical_dose: No human dosing exists (animal studies: mg/kg range)

name: SLU-PP-332 (Oral)
strength: 1 mg/tablet / 5 mg/tablet / 20 mg/tablet / 50 mg/tablet / 100 mg/capsule / 250 mcg/tablet / 500 mcg/tablet
excerpt: Oral tablet form of the ERRγ agonist SLU-PP-332.
content: Oral variant of the ERRγ exercise-mimetic research compound. No human data; oral bioavailability uncharacterised. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: SLU-PP-332 + BAM15 Blend (Oral)
excerpt: Blend of the ERRγ agonist SLU-PP-332 with the mitochondrial uncoupler BAM15.
content: Combines an exercise-mimetic with a mitochondrial uncoupler — both animal-study-only compounds with zero human safety data. Uncouplers historically carry severe toxicity risk (the DNP lesson). This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Unknown; uncoupling agents carry thermogenic toxicity risk

name: SLU-PP-915
excerpt: Second-generation ERRγ agonist related to SLU-PP-332.
content: Newer analogue in the ERRγ exercise-mimetic series; pre-clinical only, minimal public data. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: SNAP-8
excerpt: Acetyl octapeptide-3, a topical wrinkle peptide relaxing expression muscles mildly.
content: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3) is a cosmetic peptide moderating SNARE-complex-mediated muscle contraction — a weak topical analogue of the botulinum mechanism. Published data is industry-sponsored. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: SR9009 (Oral)
excerpt: REV-ERB agonist studied for circadian and metabolic effects.
content: SR9009 (Stenabolic) is a REV-ERBalpha agonist from Burris lab research showing altered circadian metabolism and endurance in mice. Extremely poor bioavailability in its base form, and no human data exists. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: SS-31
excerpt: Mitochondrial cardiolipin-stabilising peptide (elamipretide) studied in heart failure and mitochondrial disease trials.
content: SS-31 (elamipretide, Bendavia) is a tetrapeptide that binds cardiolipin on the inner mitochondrial membrane, stabilising electron-transport-chain function. It has genuine phase 2/3 trial data across heart failure, Barth syndrome and dry AMD — one of the better-studied research peptides. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Injection-site reactions; generally tolerated in trials
meta.pen_dial: At 40mg/3ml the concentration is ~13.3 mg/ml; 40mg = 3 ml (full cartridge)

studies.finding: Barth syndrome RCT met primary endpoints; heart-failure and dry-AMD programmes had mixed results.

name: Super Human Blend
excerpt: Amino acid, L-carnitine and NAC complex blend.
content: Multi-component wellness injection blend; component ingredients are well-known supplements, but the fixed injectable blend has no clinical evidence base. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Super Shred
excerpt: High-concentration (553 mg/ml) lipotropic injection blend.
content: Multi-component lipotropic blend at high concentration; no clinical evidence base for the fixed formulation. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: SZ352
excerpt: Proprietary cognitive-support blend (352 mg/ml) with limited public composition data.
content: Little verifiable public information exists on this blend's composition or evidence base; treat any circulating protocol as unverified. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: TB-500

studies.citation: Smart et al., Nature 2007 (thymosin beta-4 and cardiac progenitors)
studies.finding: Tb4 reactivates epicardial progenitors and improves cardiac repair in mice.
Accelerated dermal healing and angiogenesis in rodents.

bro_lore: Bro protocol: 2.0 mg twice weekly for 4-6 weeks, then weekly maintenance. Origin: equine veterinary practice scaled down. No human dosing study exists.

name: TB-500 (Oral)
excerpt: Oral formulation of thymosin beta-4 fragment.
content: TB-500's healing data is injectable-form animal work; oral bioavailability of the fragment is unquantified, so oral products are pharmacologically speculative. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Teriparatide
excerpt: PTH(1-34) analogue approved (Forteo) for osteoporosis — an actual medicine.
content: Teriparatide is recombinant parathyroid hormone 1-34, approved for osteoporosis. It is anabolic to bone in intermittent pulses — a genuinely effective, well-studied drug with defined contraindications (prior skeletal radiation, hypercalcemia risk, osteosarcoma history). This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Hypercalcemia, dizziness, injection-site reactions; osteosarcoma warning from rat studies
meta.pen_dial: Approved pens dial 20 mcg directly; research vials at 10mg/3ml are far above clinical concentration

studies.citation: Neer et al., NEJM 2001 (Forteo pivotal trial)
studies.finding: Reduced vertebral and non-vertebral fracture risk in postmenopausal osteoporosis; approval followed.

name: Tesamorelin
excerpt: GHRH analogue approved (Egrifta) for HIV-associated lipodystrophy.
content: Tesamorelin is a 44-amino-acid GHRH analogue approved in the US to reduce visceral fat in HIV lipodystrophy — one of the few peptides here with an actual regulatory approval. It stimulates endogenous GH in a pulsatile manner. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Injection-site reactions, arthralgia, oedema; avoid with active malignancy
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 2mg ≈ 0.6 ml

studies.citation: Dhillon et al., NEJM 2011 (Egrifta pivotal trial)
studies.finding: Reduced visceral adipose tissue in HIV lipodystrophy; approval followed.

name: Tesamorelin + Ipamorelin
excerpt: Blend of the approved GHRH analogue tesamorelin with the GHRP ipamorelin.
content: Pairs the only approved GHRH analogue with a selective GHRP for amplified GH pulsation. No published data supports the fixed-dose blend; component-wise pharmacology applies. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Reported protocols: 100-200 mcg ipamorelin-equivalent per dose (unverified)

name: Tesofensine (Oral)
excerpt: Triple monoamine reuptake inhibitor studied for obesity; notable for blood-pressure and mood effects.
content: Tesofensine inhibits serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine reuptake; phase 3 trials showed strong weight loss but dose-dependent hypertension and mood effects stalled development. It is a CNS drug, not a peptide, with real psychiatric contraindications. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Hypertension, insomnia, mood changes; contraindicated with cardiac disease

name: Testagen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for testicular/endocrine function.
content: Testagen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on testicular/endocrine tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: Thymalin
excerpt: Thymus-derived peptide bioregulator studied for immune restoration.
content: Thymalin is a thymic peptide preparation from the Russian pharmacopoeia, studied for immune restoration in immunodeficiency states. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 10mg = 3 ml (full cartridge)

studies.finding: Russian-language clinical use; Western replication absent.

name: Thymosin Alpha-1
excerpt: Thymic peptide approved in several countries (Zadaxin) as an immunomodulator.
content: Thymosin alpha-1 is a 28-amino-acid thymic peptide approved in several countries (as Zadaxin) for chronic hepatitis B and as an immune adjuvant, with published clinical trials. Not approved in the UK/US. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Approved regimens abroad: 1.6 mg subcutaneous twice weekly
meta.pen_dial: At 10mg/3ml the concentration is ~3333 mcg/ml; 1.6mg ≈ 0.48 ml

studies.citation: Published RCTs in chronic hepatitis B (Zadaxin programme)
studies.finding: Approved in several countries as immunomodulator; not approved in UK/US.
72-week RCT: -20.9% (15 mg) vs -3.1% placebo — the largest drug-induced loss in a phase 3 obesity trial to date.
Superior HbA1c reduction vs semaglutide and insulin comparators.

name: Tirzepatide oral tablet
excerpt: Research-grade oral formulation of tirzepatide.
content: Tirzepatide's approved forms are injectable; oral peptide delivery without an absorption enhancer has poor bioavailability, so research tablets are pharmacologically dubious. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Expected GLP-1-class GI effects; oral absorption unverified

name: Triptorelin
excerpt: Long-acting GnRH agonist that paradoxically shuts down the HPG axis; clinical use in prostate cancer and precocious puberty.
content: Triptorelin is a GnRH agonist that initially stimulates then abolishes LH/FSH production — it is used clinically to induce chemical castration in prostate cancer and to treat precocious puberty. A single misplaced informal dose can crash testosterone for weeks. The supplier's warnings are not decoration. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Clinical regimens: 3.75 mg monthly depot by indication
meta.side_effects: HPG-axis shutdown, testosterone crash, hot flushes, bone-density loss
meta.pen_dial: At 2mg/3ml the concentration is ~667 mcg/ml; clinical dosing is not informal-dose compatible

studies.finding: Established clinical GnRH-agonist use; informal misuse risks weeks-long HPG shutdown.

name: Vesugen
excerpt: Short-peptide bioregulator studied for vascular endothelium function.
content: Vesugen is a Khavinson-series peptide bioregulator claimed to act on vascular endothelium tissue by modulating gene expression. Khavinson-series short peptide bioregulator studied mainly in Russian literature; Western replication is limited. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.pen_dial: At 20mg/3ml the concentration is ~6667 mcg/ml; 1mg ≈ 0.15 ml

name: VIP
excerpt: Vasoactive intestinal peptide — 28-residue neuropeptide with potent vasodilatory and anti-inflammatory effects.
content: VIP is a 28-amino-acid neuropeptide with vasodilatory, smooth-muscle-relaxing and immunomodulatory roles. Research covers pulmonary hypertension, inflammatory conditions and circadian biology. Very short plasma half-life. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.typical_dose: Trial regimens: infusion-based; no informal regimen

name: Water (supplier specification)
excerpt: Sterile water for injection.
content: Plain sterile water, no preservative — single-use only once punctured, unlike BAC water. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

name: Wolverine Blend
excerpt: BPC-157 + TB-500 blend — the classic healing stack.
content: The two most-informally-used healing peptides in one vial. No published clinical data for the co-formulation; component pharmacology and caveats apply. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.
bro_lore: Bro protocol: component-equivalent daily dosing. Origin: grey-market blend marketing; no clinical data for the co-formulation.

name: YK-11 (Oral)
excerpt: SARM-like compound that also induces follistatin via myostatin-pathway interference.
content: YK-11 is a steroidal compound classified as a SARM but acting partly through follistatin induction (myostatin axis). Almost no reliable biological data exists; hepatotoxicity concerns follow from its steroid backbone. This entry is informational only and is not a recommendation.

meta.side_effects: Suppression of natural testosterone, lipid changes, liver enzyme elevation; long-term data absent; possible hepatotoxicity
